claim: The majority of adult hippocampal newborn cells die during early differentiation from intermediate progenitors (IPCs) to immature neurons.
source: The majority of adult hippocampal newborn cells die during early differentiation from intermediate progenitors (IPCs) to immature neurons.
evidence: This is a statement in the abstract that is supported by citations in the introduction and data presented in the results.

claim: Neural stem cells in vivo are located in a relative hypoxic environment.
source: Neural stem cells in vivo are located in a relative hypoxic environment, and hypoxia enhances their survival, proliferation and stemness in vitro.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature and by the pimonidazole staining data presented in Figure 1.

claim: Hypoxia enhances neural stem cell survival, proliferation and stemness in vitro.
source: Neural stem cells in vivo are located in a relative hypoxic environment, and hypoxia enhances their survival, proliferation and stemness in vitro.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature and by the neurosphere data in Figure 7.

claim: Migration of IPCs away from hypoxic zones within the SGZ might result in oxidative damage, thus triggering cell death.
source: Thus, we hypothesized that migration of IPCs away from hypoxic zones within the SGZ might result in oxidative damage, thus triggering cell death.
evidence: This is presented as a hypothesis that is then tested with 8-OHdG staining data in Figure 1.

claim: Hypoxic niches were observed along the SGZ, composed of adult NSCs and early IPCs.
source: Hypoxic niches were observed along the SGZ, composed of adult NSCs and early IPCs, and oxidative byproducts were present in adjacent late IPCs and neuroblasts.
evidence: This is supported by pimonidazole staining data shown in Figure 1B-D.

claim: Oxidative byproducts were present in adjacent late IPCs and neuroblasts.
source: Hypoxic niches were observed along the SGZ, composed of adult NSCs and early IPCs, and oxidative byproducts were present in adjacent late IPCs and neuroblasts.
evidence: This is supported by 8-OHdG staining data shown in Figure 1E-F.

claim: Stabilizing hypoxia inducible factor-1α with dimethyloxallyl glycine increased early survival, but not proliferation or differentiation, in neurospheres in vitro.
source: Stabilizing hypoxia inducible factor-1α with dimethyloxallyl glycine increased early survival, but not proliferation or differentiation, in neurospheres in vitro and in newly born SGZ cells in vivo.
evidence: This is supported by neurosphere assay data in Figure 7.

claim: Stabilizing hypoxia inducible factor-1α with dimethyloxallyl glycine increased early survival, but not proliferation or differentiation, in newly born SGZ cells in vivo.
source: Stabilizing hypoxia inducible factor-1α with dimethyloxallyl glycine increased early survival, but not proliferation or differentiation, in neurospheres in vitro and in newly born SGZ cells in vivo.
evidence: This is supported by BrdU labeling data in Figures 3 and 4.

claim: Localized hypoxia within the SGZ contributes to the neurogenic microenvironment.
source: We propose that localized hypoxia within the SGZ contributes to the neurogenic microenvironment and determines the early, activity-independent survival of adult hippocampal newborn cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Localized hypoxia within the SGZ determines the early, activity-independent survival of adult hippocampal newborn cells.
source: We propose that localized hypoxia within the SGZ contributes to the neurogenic microenvironment and determines the early, activity-independent survival of adult hippocampal newborn cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined experimental data, including electrophysiology showing lack of synaptic activity at 3 days and DMOG effects on survival.

claim: In the subgranular zone (SGZ) of the adult hippocampal dentate gyrus (DG), new neurons are continuously generated throughout adulthood.
source: In the subgranular zone (SGZ) of the adult hippocampal dentate gyrus (DG), one of the two neurogenic niches in the adult mammalian brain, new neurons are continuously generated throughout adulthood (Taupin and Gage, 2002; van Praag et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: The SGZ is one of the two neurogenic niches in the adult mammalian brain.
source: In the subgranular zone (SGZ) of the adult hippocampal dentate gyrus (DG), one of the two neurogenic niches in the adult mammalian brain, new neurons are continuously generated throughout adulthood (Taupin and Gage, 2002; van Praag et al., 2002).
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field, supported by citations.

claim: Adult hippocampal neurogenesis is a highly dynamic and regulated process that evolves slowly over several weeks.
source: Adult hippocampal neurogenesis is a highly dynamic and regulated process that evolves slowly over several weeks (Zhao et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Adult neural stem/radial glia-like cells (Type I cells) reside at the interface between the SGZ and the hilus.
source: Adult neural stem/ radial glia-like cells (Type I cells) reside at the interface between the SGZ and the hilus, and give rise to rapidly dividing intermediate progenitors (Type 2 cells).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature describing the neurogenic lineage.

claim: Adult neural stem cells give rise to rapidly dividing intermediate progenitors (Type 2 cells).
source: Adult neural stem/ radial glia-like cells (Type I cells) reside at the interface between the SGZ and the hilus, and give rise to rapidly dividing intermediate progenitors (Type 2 cells).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature describing the neurogenic lineage.

claim: Type 2 intermediate progenitors migrate a short distance into the SGZ and progressively differentiate into neuroblasts (Type 3 cells).
source: These cells migrate a short distance into the SGZ and progressively (via Type 2a and Type 2b intermediate progenitors) differentiate into neuroblasts (Type 3 cells) (Zhao et al., 2008; Fuentealba et al., 2012; Bonaguidi et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature describing the neurogenic lineage.

claim: Neuroblasts exit the cell cycle and become immature granule cell neurons.
source: Neuroblasts then exit the cell cycle and become immature granule cell neurons, which in turn migrate into the granule cell layer and incorporate into the pre-existing functional hippocampal circuits (Toni et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Immature granule cell neurons migrate into the granule cell layer and incorporate into the pre-existing functional hippocampal circuits.
source: Neuroblasts then exit the cell cycle and become immature granule cell neurons, which in turn migrate into the granule cell layer and incorporate into the pre-existing functional hippocampal circuits (Toni et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: In the young adult mouse DG as many as 4000 new cells are born daily.
source: In the young adult mouse DG as many as 4000 new cells are born daily, but only a subset (~30%) survive at 4 weeks post-mitosis to become mature granule cell neurons (Dayer et al., 2003; Kempermann, 2003; Kempermann et al., 2006; Sierra et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Only a subset (~30%) of newborn cells survive at 4 weeks post-mitosis to become mature granule cell neurons.
source: In the young adult mouse DG as many as 4000 new cells are born daily, but only a subset (~30%) survive at 4 weeks post-mitosis to become mature granule cell neurons (Dayer et al., 2003; Kempermann, 2003; Kempermann et al., 2006; Sierra et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The survival of adult-generated granule cells exhibits two critical periods.
source: The survival of adult-generated granule cells exhibits two critical periods; an early one during the transition from transient amplifying progenitors to neuroblasts and a later one during the integration of the immature neurons (Dayer et al., 2003; Kempermann, 2003; Sierra et al., 2010; Mandyam et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: An early critical period for survival occurs during the transition from transient amplifying progenitors to neuroblasts.
source: The survival of adult-generated granule cells exhibits two critical periods; an early one during the transition from transient amplifying progenitors to neuroblasts and a later one during the integration of the immature neurons (Dayer et al., 2003; Kempermann, 2003; Sierra et al., 2010; Mandyam et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: A later critical period for survival occurs during the integration of the immature neurons.
source: The survival of adult-generated granule cells exhibits two critical periods; an early one during the transition from transient amplifying progenitors to neuroblasts and a later one during the integration of the immature neurons (Dayer et al., 2003; Kempermann, 2003; Sierra et al., 2010; Mandyam et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The early phase of cell death is associated with phagocytosis of apoptotic cells by microglia.
source: The early phase is associated with phagocytosis of apoptotic cells by microglia (Sierra et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: GABA-mediated-depolarization and NMDA-receptor-mediated neuronal activity regulate the later phase of survival, at two and three weeks after mitosis respectively.
source: GABA-mediated-depolarization and NMDA-receptor-mediated neuronal activity regulate the later phase of survival, at two and three weeks after mitosis respectively (Jagasia et al., 2009; Tashiro et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Less is known about the mechanisms responsible for the early death of newborn granule cells which occurs during the first days post mitosis.
source: However, less is known about the mechanisms responsible for the early death of newborn granule cells which occurs during the first days post mitosis, as cells exit the specialized microenvironment (NSC niche) of the adult SGZ.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge in the field, supported by inference from the literature.

claim: Differential oxygen tensions may be an important component of the NSC niche.
source: There is increasing evidence that differential oxygen tensions may be an important component of the NSC niche and that oxygen sensing can regulate the proliferation, survival and differentiation of neural stem cells and progenitors (Panchision, 2009; de Filippis and Delia, 2011; Mazumdar et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Oxygen sensing can regulate the proliferation, survival and differentiation of neural stem cells and progenitors.
source: There is increasing evidence that differential oxygen tensions may be an important component of the NSC niche and that oxygen sensing can regulate the proliferation, survival and differentiation of neural stem cells and progenitors (Panchision, 2009; de Filippis and Delia, 2011; Mazumdar et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Pimonidazole is reductively activated and binds only to cells that have oxygen concentrations less than 14 μM, equivalent to a pO2 of 10 mm Hg (1.3% O2).
source: Pimonidazole (PH) is reductively activated and binds only to cells that have oxygen concentrations less than 14 μM, equivalent to a pO2 of 10 mm Hg (1.3% O2) (Raleigh et al., 1998).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature describing the properties of pimonidazole.

claim: Pimonidazole labeled hypoxic cells or groups of cells along the inner border of the SGZ.
source: Pimonidazole labeled hypoxic cells or groups of cells along the inner border of the SGZ (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by the immunostaining data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: 71.7 ± 10.4% of the hypoxic cells were radial glia (GFAP+).
source: Double labeling with selective markers revealed that the majority (71.7 ± 10.4%) of the hypoxic cells were radial glia (GFAP+) and a smaller percentage (28.3 ± 9.5%) were early intermediate progenitor cells (Tbr2+/Dcx-) (Figure 1C,D) in close proximity to the SGZ.
evidence: This is supported by quantification of double-labeling immunostaining data shown in Figure 1C,D.

claim: 28.3 ± 9.5% of the hypoxic cells were early intermediate progenitor cells (Tbr2+/Dcx-).
source: Double labeling with selective markers revealed that the majority (71.7 ± 10.4%) of the hypoxic cells were radial glia (GFAP+) and a smaller percentage (28.3 ± 9.5%) were early intermediate progenitor cells (Tbr2+/Dcx-) (Figure 1C,D) in close proximity to the SGZ.
evidence: This is supported by quantification of double-labeling immunostaining data shown in Figure 1C,D.

claim: None of the hypoxic cells (0%) expressed the neuroblast marker doublecortin (DCX).
source: In contrast, none of the hypoxic cells (0%) expressed the neuroblast marker doublecortin (DCX, Figure 1C,D).
evidence: This is supported by quantification of double-labeling immunostaining data shown in Figure 1C,D.

claim: 74.6 ± 5.8% of the 8-OHdG positive cells were late intermediate progenitors (Tbr2+/DCX+).
source: Interestingly, phenotypic analysis revealed that 74.6 ± 5.8% of the 8-OHdG positive cells were late intermediate progenitors (Tbr2+/DCX+) and 29.2 ± 12.2% were neuroblasts (DCX+ only) (Figure 1E,F).
evidence: This is supported by quantification of immunostaining data shown in Figure 1E,F.

claim: 29.2 ± 12.2% of the 8-OHdG positive cells were neuroblasts (DCX+ only).
source: Interestingly, phenotypic analysis revealed that 74.6 ± 5.8% of the 8-OHdG positive cells were late intermediate progenitors (Tbr2+/DCX+) and 29.2 ± 12.2% were neuroblasts (DCX+ only) (Figure 1E,F).
evidence: This is supported by quantification of immunostaining data shown in Figure 1E,F.

claim: A subset of newborn cells in the SGZ undergoes oxidative damage during their early migration and differentiation.
source: Thus, a subset of newborn cells in the SGZ undergoes oxidative damage during their early migration and differentiation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the 8-OHdG staining data in Figure 1E,F.

claim: The most critical survival period for adult-generated dentate granule cells occurs during the first few days post mitosis, as they differentiate from late intermediate progenitors to neuroblasts.
source: The most critical survival period for adult-generated dentate granule cells occurs during the first few days post mitosis, as they differentiate from late intermediate progenitors to neuroblasts (Dayer et al., 2003; Kempermann, 2003; Sierra et al., 2010; Mandyam et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: DMOG suppresses propyl hydroxylase, thus stabilizing/enhancing HIF-1α activity under normoxic conditions.
source: Hypoxia Inducible Factor-1 α (HIF-1α), the master regulator of oxygen homeostasis, is enzymatically degraded under normoxia by propyl hydroxylases (Semenza, 2001). DMOG suppresses propyl hydroxylase, thus stabilizing/enhancing HIF-1α activity under normoxic conditions (Harten et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature describing the mechanism of DMOG.

claim: HIF-1α is enzymatically degraded under normoxia by propyl hydroxylases.
source: Hypoxia Inducible Factor-1 α (HIF-1α), the master regulator of oxygen homeostasis, is enzymatically degraded under normoxia by propyl hydroxylases (Semenza, 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: HIF-1α is the master regulator of oxygen homeostasis.
source: Hypoxia Inducible Factor-1 α (HIF-1α), the master regulator of oxygen homeostasis, is enzymatically degraded under normoxia by propyl hydroxylases (Semenza, 2001).
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field, supported by citation.

claim: DMOG treatment elevated mRNA levels of HIF-1α and its downstream targets VEGF, EPO and LEF-1.
source: Consistent with stabilization of HIF-1α by DMOG, mRNA levels of HIF-1α as well as its downstream targets VEGF, EPO and LEF-1, were significantly higher after 3 days of DMOG treatment (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: DMOG treatment increased HIF-1α protein levels (p = 0.03).
source: As expected given the effect on downstream targets, DMOG treatment also increased HIF-1α protein levels (Figure 2B, p = 0.03).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The increase in HIF1α mRNA levels occurs because of autoregulation of transcription by hypoxia response elements in the HIF1α promoter.
source: The increase in HIF1α mRNA levels occurs because of autoregulation of transcription by hypoxia response elements in the HIF1α promoter (Iyer et al., 1998).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Hypoxia increases phosphorylation of Akt (Ser473), a serine/threonine kinase that promotes cell survival and reduces apoptosis.
source: Hypoxia also increases phosphorylation of Akt (Ser473), a serine/threonine kinase that promotes cell survival and reduces apoptosis (Beitner-Johnson et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: DMOG treatment induced a two-fold increase in the number of phospho-AKT+/DCX+ cells relative to vehicle treated animals (p = 0.01).
source: Double immunohistochemistry with an antibody that specifically recognizes phosphorylated Akt together with an antibody against the neuroblast/immature neuron marker doublecortin (DCX) (Figure 2C left panels), revealed that DMOG treatment induced a two-fold increase in the number of phospho-AKT+/DCX+ cells relative to vehicle treated animals (p = 0.01, n = 3 animals, Figure 2C right panel), also consistent with the hypoxia mimetic action of DMOG.
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: There was no significant effect of DMOG on the net proliferation of newborn cells at 3 dpi (p = 0.5).
source: There was no significant effect of DMOG on the net proliferation of newborn cells at 3 dpi. (control group, 12901 ± 1870 Ki67+ cells/mm3, n = 5 animals, DMOG group 11859 ± 2953 Ki67+ cells/mm3, n = 5 animals, p = 0.5, Figure 3A,B,E).
evidence: This is supported by Ki67 immunostaining data shown in Figure 3A,B,E.

claim: There was not a detectable effect of DMOG on the total density of Tbr2+ cells (p = 0.07).
source: Similarly, there was not a detectable effect on the total density of Tbr2+ cells (control group: 5776 ± 681 cells/mm3, DMOG: 7331 ± 1381 cells/mm3, p = 0.07, n = 5 animals).
evidence: This is supported by Tbr2 immunostaining data.

claim: At 3 dpi. 43.9 ± 5.8% of the proliferating cells were neural stem cells, nestin-only expressing cells, and 55.3 ± 7.1% were intermediate progenitors expressing both nestin and DCX.
source: At 3 dpi. 43.9 ± 5.8% of the proliferating cells were neural stem cells, nestin-only expressing cells, and 55.3 ± 7.1% were intermediate progenitors expressing both nestin and DCX (n = 4 animals).
evidence: This is supported by triple-labeling immunostaining data.

claim: DMOG did not cause a shift in the proliferative populations of SGZ progenitor at 3 dpi (p = 0.56).
source: DMOG did not cause a shift in the proliferative populations of SGZ progenitor at 3 dpi. (41.9 ± 9.53% Ki67+/Nestin+, 58.1 ± 8.33 Ki67+/Nestin+/DCX+, 2-way ANOVA, n = 4 animals, p = 0.56, Figure 3C,D,F).
evidence: This is supported by triple-labeling immunostaining data shown in Figure 3C,D,F.

claim: The composition of the progenitor subtypes, measured as a percentage of BrdU+ cells was unaffected by DMOG treatment at 3, 7, 14, 21 and 28 days post-injection (p >0.99).
source: The composition of the progenitor subtypes, measured as a percentage of BrdU+ cells was unaffected by DMOG treatment at 3, 7, 14, 21 and 28 days post-injection (2-way ANOVA, no interaction between vehicle and DMOG groups, p >0.99).
evidence: This is supported by BrdU labeling and phenotypic analysis data shown in Figure 3G.

claim: DMOG had no effect on the total volume of the dentate gyrus (p = 0.89).
source: DMOG had no effect on the total volume of the dentate gyrus (Control: 0.61 mm3 ± 0.02, n = 3 animals, DMOG: 0.59 ± 0.04, n = animals, p = 0.89), indicating that there were no macroscopic changes in the tissue.
evidence: This is supported by volumetric analysis data.

claim: DMOG resulted in an increase of BrdU labeled nuclei in the SGZ.
source: DMOG resulted in an increase of BrdU labeled nuclei in the SGZ (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by BrdU immunostaining data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Quantitative analysis of the BrdU+ cells showed a significant effect of DMOG on survival of newborn cells in the SGZ (p = 0.0002).
source: Quantitative analysis of the BrdU+ cells showed a significant effect of DMOG on survival of newborn cells in the SGZ (2-way ANOVA, p = 0.0002, Figure 4C).
evidence: This is supported by quantification of BrdU+ cells shown in Figure 4C.

claim: One day of DMOG treatment did not alter the number of BrdU+ cells (p = 0.49).
source: One day of DMOG treatment did not alter the number of BrdU+ cells, consistent with no effect on proliferation (p = 0.49, n = 6 animals, Figure 4C).
evidence: This is supported by quantification of BrdU+ cells shown in Figure 4C.

claim: DMOG significantly increased the survival of BrdU+ cells by 3 days post-mitosis (p <0.0001).
source: However, DMOG significantly increased the survival of BrdU+ cells by 3 days post-mitosis (p <0.0001, n = 12 animals).
evidence: This is supported by quantification of BrdU+ cells shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The relative increase in BrdU-labelled cells in DMOG persisted at later time points (7 dpi., p = 0.0017; 14 dpi., p = 0.003; 21 dpi., p = 0.007; 28 dpi., p = 0.01).
source: Interestingly, the relative increase in BrdU-labelled cells in DMOG persisted at later time points (7 dpi., p = 0.0017, n = 8 animals; 14 dpi., p = 0.003, n = 6; 21 dpi., p = 0.007, n = 6; 28 dpi., p = 0.01, n = 6), as assessed by the rate of BrdU+ cell loss between 3 and 28 dpi. (Comparison of fits, p = 0.5, F = 0.7).
evidence: This is supported by quantification of BrdU+ cells shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Exposure to DMOG for the first three day post-mitosis resulted in a 33% increase in survival (p = 0.023).
source: Exposure to DMOG for the first three day post-mitosis resulted in a 33% increase in survival (p = 0.023, n = 3), whereas exposure for 7 days did not yield a significant further increase (p = 0.23, n = 3).
evidence: This is supported by quantification of BrdU+ cells at 28 dpi shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Exposure to DMOG for 7 days did not yield a significant further increase in survival compared to 3 days (p = 0.23).
source: Exposure to DMOG for the first three day post-mitosis resulted in a 33% increase in survival (p = 0.023, n = 3), whereas exposure for 7 days did not yield a significant further increase (p = 0.23, n = 3).
evidence: This is supported by quantification of BrdU+ cells at 28 dpi shown in Figure 4D.

claim: DMOG administration from day 7–14 had no effect on newborn cell survival (p = 0.76).
source: However, DMOG administration from day 7–14, a critical period during which the newborn cells begin to integrate into the hippocampal network, had no effect on their survival (p = 0.76, n = 3).
evidence: This is supported by quantification of BrdU+ cells at 28 dpi shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The differentiation of BrdU+ cells into mature neurons (NeuN+) by 28 dpi. was not affected by exposure to DMOG for either the first 3 or 7 days post mitosis (p = 0.8).
source: The differentiation of BrdU+ cells into mature neurons (NeuN+) by 28 dpi. was not affected by exposure to DMOG for either the first 3 or 7 days post mitosis (BrdU+NeuN+/BrdU+: 0–3 days, Vehicle: 96 ± 4%, DMOG: 95 ± 2%, n = 3; 0–7 days, Vehicle: 98 ± 3%, DMOG: 96 ± 2%, n = 3, 2-way ANOVA p = 0.8).
evidence: This is supported by quantification of BrdU+/NeuN+ cells.

claim: The hypoxia mimetic agent DMOG does not alter the proliferation or differentiation of newborn cells in the adult DG, but rather specifically promotes their survival during the first few days post-mitosis.
source: The above results indicate that the hypoxia mimetic agent DMOG does not alter the proliferation or differentiation of newborn cells in the adult DG, but rather specifically promotes their survival during the first few days post-mitosis, during their transition from intermediate progenitors to neuroblasts.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined experimental data in Figures 3 and 4.

claim: The pro-apoptotic gene Bax mediates programmed cell death of adult-generated hippocampal cells.
source: Because the pro-apoptotic gene Bax mediates programmed cell death of adult-generated hippocampal cells (Sun, 2004; Sahay et al., 2011), we hypothesized that DMOG treatment should not affect the survival of cells lacking Bax.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The ratio of Cre-GFP/ mCherry cells was increased in vehicle treated Baxfl/fl compared to WT animals at 7 dpi (31.7 ± 10.3%, p = 0.002).
source: The ratio of Cre-GFP/ mCherry cells was increased in vehicle treated Baxfl/fl compared to WT animals at 7 dpi. (Figure 5B,C, 31.7 ± 10.3%, p = 0.002), indicating that loss of Bax augments the survival of adult-born cells at one week post-mitosis.
evidence: This is supported by quantification of retrovirus-labeled cells shown in Figure 5B,C.

claim: Loss of Bax augments the survival of adult-born cells at one week post-mitosis.
source: The ratio of Cre-GFP/ mCherry cells was increased in vehicle treated Baxfl/fl compared to WT animals at 7 dpi. (Figure 5B,C, 31.7 ± 10.3%, p = 0.002), indicating that loss of Bax augments the survival of adult-born cells at one week post-mitosis.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the retrovirus labeling data in Figure 5B,C.

claim: Treatment with DMOG for 7 days post injection decreased the Cre-GFP/ mCherry ratio compared to Baxfl/fl vehicle treated animals (30 ± 9.4%, p = 0.03).
source: Treatment with DMOG for 7 days post injection decreased the Cre-GFP/ mCherry ratio compared to Baxfl/fl vehicle treated animals (Figure 5B,C, 30 ± 9.4%, p = 0.03), consistent with a DMOG-mediated increase in survival in mCherry+ cells.
evidence: This is supported by quantification of retrovirus-labeled cells shown in Figure 5B,C.

claim: Activation of HIF-1α signaling enhances the early phase of survival of the newborn cells in the adult DG.
source: Together our results strongly suggest activation of HIF-1α signaling enhances the early phase of survival of the newborn cells in the adult DG.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined experimental data including DMOG effects and Bax rescue experiments.

claim: None of the 3 day-old cells had any spontaneous post-synaptic currents (PSCs) in >5 min of continuous recording per cell (n = 11).
source: Strikingly, none of these cells in wildtype animals had any spontaneous post-synaptic currents (PSCs) in >5 min of continuous recording per cell (n = 11), compared to an sPSC frequency of 0.55 ± 0.15 Hz in adjacent mature cells (n = 4).
evidence: This is supported by whole-cell voltage clamp recordings from retrovirus-labeled cells.

claim: Adjacent mature cells had an sPSC frequency of 0.55 ± 0.15 Hz (n = 4).
source: Strikingly, none of these cells in wildtype animals had any spontaneous post-synaptic currents (PSCs) in >5 min of continuous recording per cell (n = 11), compared to an sPSC frequency of 0.55 ± 0.15 Hz in adjacent mature cells (n = 4).
evidence: This is supported by whole-cell voltage clamp recordings from mature granule cells.

claim: None of the 3 day-old cells had any evoked synaptic responses in the middle molecular layer (n = 11).
source: Furthermore, none of the 3 day-old cells had any evoked synaptic responses in the middle molecular layer ( >ten 10-second 8 Hz trains per cell, n = 11; Figure 6A), despite robust extracellular field potentials in these same slices at the same stimulation intensity (n = 7, data not shown) or large PSCs in neighboring mature cells (n = 4; Figure 6B).
evidence: This is supported by whole-cell voltage clamp recordings with afferent stimulation shown in Figure 6A.

claim: There is minimal, if any, synaptic innervation at 3 days post-mitosis.
source: Together, these results indicate that there is minimal, if any, synaptic innervation at this maturational stage.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the electrophysiology data in Figure 6A,B.

claim: DMOG did not affect neuronal activity in immature or mature DG granule cells as measured by immunohistochemistry for the immediate early genes pCREB or c-Fos.
source: Likewise DMOG did not affect neuronal activity in immature or mature DG granule cells as measured by immunohistochemistry for the immediate early genes pCREB or c-Fos (Figure 6C,D), which are widely used as surrogate markers for neural activity (Jagasia et al., 2009; Lonze and Ginty, 2002).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 6C,D.

claim: DMOG treatment did not affect the number of p-CREB+ cells (p = 0.35).
source: Labeled cells were quantified as follows: pCREB - (control group, 122535 ± 19273 p-CREB+ cells/mm3, n = 4 animals, DMOG group 134051 ± 9733 p-CREB+ cells/mm3, n = 4 animals, p = 0.35)
evidence: This is supported by quantification of p-CREB immunostaining.

claim: DMOG treatment did not affect the number of c-Fos+ cells (p = 0.9).
source: c-Fos - (control group, 20175 ± 1025 c-Fos+ cells/mm3, n = 4 animals; DMOG group 20646 ± 2766 c-fos+ cells/mm3, n = 4 animals; p = 0.9).
evidence: This is supported by quantification of c-Fos immunostaining.

claim: DMOG treatment did not affect neuronal activity in the hilus as assayed by double immunohistochemistry with c-Fos and GAD-67 (p = 0.4).
source: DMOG treatment also did not affect neuronal activity in the hilus as assayed by double immunohistochemistry with c-Fos and the GABAergic neuronal marker glutamic acid decarboxylase-64 (Gad-67). We detected only sparse activation of hilar mossy cells (Fos+ only) or hilar interneurons (Fos+/GAD67+) under basal conditions, which was unaffected by DMOG (Vehicle, Fos+: 144 ± 55 cells/mm3, Fos+/GAD67+: 14 ± 16 cells/mm3, n = 4; DMOG, Fos only+: 116 ± 14 cells/mm3, n = 4, Fos+/GAD67+: 13 ± 14 cells/mm3, n = 4, p = 0.4)
evidence: This is supported by quantification of c-Fos/GAD-67 double immunostaining.

claim: Stabilization and activation of HIF-1a signaling by DMOG rescues early survival of newborn cells in an activity-independent manner.
source: These results indicate that stabilization and activation of HIF-1a signaling by DMOG rescues early survival of newborn cells in an activity-independent manner.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined electrophysiology and activity marker data in Figure 6.

claim: Adult DG neurospheres cultured under all three conditions (normoxia, DMOG, hypoxia) exhibited normal morphology, each containing committed progenitors that co-expressed nestin and doublecortin.
source: Neurospheres under all three conditions exhibited normal morphology, each containing committed progenitors that co-expressed nestin and doublecortin (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is supported by immunocytochemistry data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Treatment with DMOG increased the number of neurospheres (p = 0.01).
source: Treatment with DMOG or reducing O2 levels to 2.5% increased the number of neurospheres, a measure of cell survival (p = 0.01 and p = 0.002 respectively), but had no effect on the size of the neurospheres, a measure of cells' proliferation (p = 0.98, Figure 7B,C).
evidence: This is supported by quantification of neurosphere number shown in Figure 7C.

claim: Reducing O2 levels to 2.5% increased the number of neurospheres (p = 0.002).
source: Treatment with DMOG or reducing O2 levels to 2.5% increased the number of neurospheres, a measure of cell survival (p = 0.01 and p = 0.002 respectively), but had no effect on the size of the neurospheres, a measure of cells' proliferation (p = 0.98, Figure 7B,C).
evidence: This is supported by quantification of neurosphere number shown in Figure 7C.

claim: DMOG and hypoxia had no effect on the size of the neurospheres (p = 0.98).
source: Treatment with DMOG or reducing O2 levels to 2.5% increased the number of neurospheres, a measure of cell survival (p = 0.01 and p = 0.002 respectively), but had no effect on the size of the neurospheres, a measure of cells' proliferation (p = 0.98, Figure 7B,C).
evidence: This is supported by quantification of neurosphere diameter shown in Figure 7B.

claim: DMOG reduced the percentage of apoptotic cells in neurospheres as measured by caspase-3 immunoreactivity (normoxia: 28.1 ± 1.7%; DMOG: 17.7 ± 2.6%, p = 0.01).
source: Consistent with enhanced survival DMOG or hypoxia reduced the percentage of apoptotic cells in neurospheres as measured by caspase-3 immunoreactivity (normoxia: 28.1 ± 1.7%; DMOG: 17.7 ± 2.6%, p = 0.01; hypoxia: 11.4 ± 2.3%, p <0.0001, Figure 7D–G).
evidence: This is supported by quantification of activated caspase-3 immunostaining shown in Figure 7D-G.

claim: Hypoxia reduced the percentage of apoptotic cells in neurospheres as measured by caspase-3 immunoreactivity (hypoxia: 11.4 ± 2.3%, p <0.0001).
source: Consistent with enhanced survival DMOG or hypoxia reduced the percentage of apoptotic cells in neurospheres as measured by caspase-3 immunoreactivity (normoxia: 28.1 ± 1.7%; DMOG: 17.7 ± 2.6%, p = 0.01; hypoxia: 11.4 ± 2.3%, p <0.0001, Figure 7D–G).
evidence: This is supported by quantification of activated caspase-3 immunostaining shown in Figure 7D-G.

claim: No pimonidazole binding was detected in neurospheres cultured in standard atmospheric culture conditions or in the presence of DMOG.
source: No pimonidazole binding was detected in neurospheres cultured in standard atmospheric culture conditions or in the presence of DMOG, whereas only a small percentage of PH+ cells (10.8 ± 4.4%), were detected in neurospheres cultured in 2.5% O2 (Figure 7H–K), indicating that PH labeling occurs at O2 ≤2.5%.
evidence: This is supported by pimonidazole immunostaining data shown in Figure 7H-K.

claim: Only a small percentage of PH+ cells (10.8 ± 4.4%) were detected in neurospheres cultured in 2.5% O2.
source: No pimonidazole binding was detected in neurospheres cultured in standard atmospheric culture conditions or in the presence of DMOG, whereas only a small percentage of PH+ cells (10.8 ± 4.4%), were detected in neurospheres cultured in 2.5% O2 (Figure 7H–K), indicating that PH labeling occurs at O2 ≤2.5%.
evidence: This is supported by pimonidazole immunostaining data shown in Figure 7H-K.

claim: PH labeling occurs at O2 ≤2.5%.
source: No pimonidazole binding was detected in neurospheres cultured in standard atmospheric culture conditions or in the presence of DMOG, whereas only a small percentage of PH+ cells (10.8 ± 4.4%), were detected in neurospheres cultured in 2.5% O2 (Figure 7H–K), indicating that PH labeling occurs at O2 ≤2.5%.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the pimonidazole staining data in neurospheres.

claim: Hypoxia is an essential factor for the survival of DG-derived intermediate progenitors in vitro.
source: Consistent with our in vivo experiments, our neurosphere data results strongly suggest that hypoxia is an essential factor for the survival of DG-derived intermediate progenitors in vitro.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the neurosphere data in Figure 7.

claim: The partial oxygen pressure (pO2) and concentration in brain tissue is well below the 40 mm Hg in venous blood exiting the brain and is also heterogeneous.
source: The partial oxygen pressure (pO2) and concentration in brain tissue is well below the 40 mm Hg in venous blood exiting the brain and is also heterogeneous (Erecińska and Silver, 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: In rat hippocampus the pO2 has been estimated to be 20.3 mmHg.
source: In rat hippocampus the pO2 has been estimated to be 20.3 mmHg (Erecińska and Silver, 2001), whereas even more hypoxic regions have been detected in the SGZ of the adult mouse DG (Mazumdar et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Even more hypoxic regions have been detected in the SGZ of the adult mouse DG.
source: In rat hippocampus the pO2 has been estimated to be 20.3 mmHg (Erecińska and Silver, 2001), whereas even more hypoxic regions have been detected in the SGZ of the adult mouse DG (Mazumdar et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Not all cells in the SGZ were pimonidazole-labeled, but were localized to narrow zones of a few cell diameters wide along the hilar border of the SGZ.
source: Interestingly, not all cells in the SGZ were labeled, but were localized to narrow zones of a few cell diameters wide along the hilar border of the SGZ.
evidence: This is an observation from the pimonidazole staining data in Figure 1.

claim: Only a fraction of GFAP+ or Tbr2+ cells were pimonidazole-positive.
source: Only a fraction of GFAP+ or Tbr2+ cells were pimonidazole-positive whereas the hypoxic cell did not label with the proliferating marker Ki67 (data not shown).
evidence: This is an observation from the pimonidazole double-labeling data.

claim: Hypoxic cells did not label with the proliferating marker Ki67.
source: Only a fraction of GFAP+ or Tbr2+ cells were pimonidazole-positive whereas the hypoxic cell did not label with the proliferating marker Ki67 (data not shown).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from unpublished data.

claim: Heterogeneous zones of tissue pO2 may reflect some degree of cell-state specificity as well as local metabolic demand that changes constantly even within a small specific area/volume of the brain.
source: Thus heterogeneous zones of tissue pO2 may reflect some degree of cell-state specificity as well as local metabolic demand that changes constantly even within a small specific area/volume of the brain.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the pimonidazole staining patterns.

claim: The two major determinants for tissue oxygen concentration are blood flow (oxygen supply) and oxygen consumption rate (cellularity).
source: The two major determinants for tissue oxygen concentration are blood flow (oxygen supply) and oxygen consumption rate (cellularity).
evidence: This is established knowledge about tissue oxygen dynamics.

claim: Oxygen consumption rate may predominate in the SGZ with its high ratio of nuclei to blood vessels compared to other brain regions.
source: The latter may predominate in the SGZ with its high ratio of nuclei to blood vessels compared to other brain regions (Mazumdar et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Within the SGZ zone only late amplifying progenitors (Tbr2+/DCX+) and horizontal early neuroblasts (Tbr2-/DCX+) are in direct contact with blood vessels.
source: Interestingly, a recent paper (Sun et al., 2015) revealed that within the SGZ zone only late amplifying progenitors (Tbr2+/DCX+) and horizontal early neuroblasts (Tbr2-/DCX+), among the entire population of SGZ progenitors are in direct contact with blood vessels.
evidence: This is supported by citation to a recent publication.

claim: Numerous adult stem cells reside in hypoxic niches, where they maintain a quiescent state depending predominantly on anaerobic glycolysis.
source: Numerous adult stem cells reside in hypoxic niches, where they maintain a quiescent state depending predominantly on anaerobic glycolysis (de Filippis and Delia, 2011; Mohyeldin et al., 2010; Platero-Luengo et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Stem cells exhibit different metabolic properties than their differentiated progeny that may promote 'stemness'.
source: Stem cells exhibit different metabolic properties than their differentiated progeny that may promote 'stemness'.
evidence: This is established knowledge in stem cell biology.

claim: Two-photon phosphorescence direct in vivo measurements of local oxygen tension in the bone marrow revealed a hypoxic adult stem cell niche with high heterogeneity in local pO2.
source: In either case, our results are consistent with two-photon phosphorescence direct in vivo measurements of local oxygen tension in the bone marrow, which revealed a hypoxic adult stem cell niche with high heterogeneity in local pO2 (Spencer et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: The data supports the existence of steep pO2 gradients between the neurogenic niche and the granule cell layer.
source: Thus our data supports the existence of steep pO2 gradients between the neurogenic niche and the granule cell layer.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the pimonidazole and 8-OHdG staining data.

claim: A microenvironment with low oxygen concentration confers resistance to reactive oxygen species and cytotoxic stressors.
source: Although a microenvironment with low oxygen concentration confers resistance to reactive oxygen species and cytotoxic stressors, stem cells and their progeny are susceptible to changes in redox status upon migration away from hypoxic zones (Mohyeldin et al., 2010; Platero-Luengo et al., 2014; Suda et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Stem cells and their progeny are susceptible to changes in redox status upon migration away from hypoxic zones.
source: Although a microenvironment with low oxygen concentration confers resistance to reactive oxygen species and cytotoxic stressors, stem cells and their progeny are susceptible to changes in redox status upon migration away from hypoxic zones (Mohyeldin et al., 2010; Platero-Luengo et al., 2014; Suda et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Migration of intermediate progenitors away from hypoxic zones leads to oxidative damage, and thus triggers an early phase of apoptosis.
source: This correlation suggests that migration of intermediate progenitors away from hypoxic zones leads to oxidative damage, and thus triggers an early phase of apoptosis.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the correlation between hypoxic niches and oxidative damage markers.

claim: In vitro, hypoxic conditions (defined as <5% O2) reduces apoptosis, promotes proliferation, and increases cultured embryonic, adult neural stem cells and neuronal progenitors.
source: In vitro, hypoxic conditions (defined as <5% O2) reduces apoptosis, promotes proliferation, and increases cultured embryonic, adult neural stem cells and neuronal progenitors (Sierra et al., 2010; Shingo et al., 2001; Studer et al., 2000; Felling, 2006; Gustafsson et al., 2005; Clarke and van der Kooy, 2009; Chen et al., 2007; Bürgers et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Deletion of hypoxia-inducible factor-1 alpha subunit (HIF-1α) in vivo dramatically decreased adult hippocampal neurogenesis.
source: Deletion of hypoxia-inducible factor-1 alpha subunit (HIF-1α) in vivo, a transcriptional activator mediating adaptive cellular responses to hypoxia, dramatically decreased adult hippocampal neurogenesis (Mazumdar et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Conditional ablation of HIF1-α in adult mouse brain resulted in hydrocephalus, decreased neurogenesis (partly due to an increase in apoptosis) and deficits in spatial memory.
source: Additionally, conditional ablation of HIF1-α in adult mouse brain resulted in hydrocephalus, decreased neurogenesis (partly due to an increase in apoptosis) and deficits in spatial memory (Tomita et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Transition of progenitors from a hypoxic niche to normal tissue oxygen contributes to cell death.
source: These results strongly support the idea that transition of progenitors from a hypoxic niche to normal tissue oxygen contributes to cell death.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined experimental data showing hypoxic niches, oxidative damage, and DMOG rescue effects.

claim: Only 30–50% of adult-born newborn neurons survive by 30 days post-mitosis.
source: Prior studies using mitotic markers such as BrdU found that only 30–50% of adult-born newborn neurons survive by 30 days post-mitosis (Dayer et al., 2003; Kempermann, 2003; Mandyam et al., 2007; Jagasia et al., 2009; Tashiro et al., 2006), but these studies often did not investigate survival during the first few days post-mitosis.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Adult-generated hippocampal granule cell survival is regulated mostly at the immature neuron stage (2–4 weeks post-mitosis), when is affected by neuronal activity and behavior.
source: Thus the prevailing idea, until recently, had been that adult-generated hippocampal granule cell survival is regulated mostly at the immature neuron stage (2–4 weeks post-mitosis), when is affected by neuronal activity and behavior (Jagasia et al., 2009; Tashiro et al., 2006; Gage et al., 1999).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature describing the prevailing view.

claim: There are two critical periods for survival of newborn cells in the adult SGZ, early (1–4 days post-mitosis) and late (1–3 weeks post-mitosis) with most (2/3rds) of cell death occurring in the first week.
source: Our results support two critical periods for survival of newborn cells in the adult SGZ, early (1–4 days post-mitosis) and late (1–3 weeks post-mitosis) with most (2/3rds) of cell death occurring in the first week (Dayer et al., 2003; Kempermann, 2003; Sierra et al., 2010; Mandyam et al., 2007; Jagasia et al., 2009; Tashiro et al., 2006; Mazumdar et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the current data and supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The early apoptosis is likely executed by members of the p53 and Bcl-2 protein families that are key players regulating the apoptotic machinery of adult DG neural precursors and newborn neurons.
source: The early apoptosis is likely executed by members of the p53 and Bcl-2 protein families that are key players regulating the apoptotic machinery of adult DG neural precursors and newborn neurons (Sun, 2004; Sahay et al., 2011; Cancino et al., 2013; Fatt et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: At 3 days post-mitosis, adult-born cells demonstrate no detectable neural activity.
source: Our results show that at 3 days post-mitosis, adult-born cells demonstrate no detectable neural activity.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the electrophysiology data in Figure 6.

claim: The metabolic milieu of the adult SGZ plays a critical role in the early survival of adult generated hippocampal granule cells.
source: Rather, we propose that the metabolic milieu of the adult SGZ, a previously underexplored variable of this highly specialized neurogenic niche, plays a critical role in the early survival of adult generated hippocampal granule cells.
evidence: This is the main conclusion drawn from all the experimental data presented in the manuscript.
